title: Priority mapper for performance tuning requests with SLO & cost sensitivity
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a robust priority-mapping system for incoming performance-tuning and optimization advisory requests (batching/caching knobs, quantization profiles, routing policies). Current intake routes many high-effort, low-impact asks into a single queue which causes delayed SLAs for enterprise customers. This ticket designs an intake + scoring rubric that weights SLO risks, per-token unit economics, and customer tier to produce deterministic routing to one of four lanes: Quick Tuning, Solutions Eng Advisory, Runtime Engineering Escalation, and Enterprise SLA Track.

Goals:
- Reduce triage latency (time-to-first-contact) from ~6 business days to <48 hours for enterprise and high-SLO-risk tickets.
- Auto-route >=60% of incoming requests accurately (based on manual review within first 4 weeks).
- Surface the most cost-effective knob recommendations (expected $/1k token delta) in the intake UI to accelerate Quick Tuning.
- Provide clear handoff artifacts for ENG when runtime changes are required (KV cache changes, kernel scheduling, quantization rollout).

Signals captured in intake form (minimum viable set):
- Customer name and tier (self-reported + lookup)
- Primary goal: latency reduction | cost reduction | quality parity | stability | compliance
- Current p50/p95/p99 latency and request concurrency (numbers)
- Typical sequence length (tokens) and prompt templates (link or paste)
- Model family and deployed variant (e.g., llama-2-70b-q4)
- Observed regression rate or quality tolerance (%), examples if available
- Cost per 1k tokens (estimated) and desired target cost delta
- Traffic pattern: steady | spiky | bursty | batched jobs
- Business criticality: experimental | customer-facing | SLA-bound | revenue-impacting
- Required isolation/compliance constraints (PII, encryption, region)
- Attachments: perf traces, flamegraphs, Grafana dashboard link, sample prompts

Scoring rubric (rule-based MVP):
- SLO Severity: SLA-bound=40, customer-facing=20, experimental=5
- Cost delta opportunity: >30% estimated saving=25, 10-30%=15, <10%=5
- Model/Runtime compatibility risk (engineer-estimated): high=0, medium=10, low=20
- Reproducibility of issue: reproducible=15, intermittent=5
- Customer tier: Enterprise=30, Mid-market=10, Free/Startup=0
- Compliance requirement add-on: adds +10 to Enterprise track flag
Total score interpreted as: 0-40 Quick Tuning, 41-80 Solutions Eng Advisory, 81-120 Runtime Escalation (ENG), +30 and Enterprise SLA Track override.

Routing lanes and owners:
- Quick Tuning (score <=40): Optimization Concierge (PM/DevRel) auto-suggests batching/cache knobs, quick quantization toggles; target TTF contact <24h; owner: Optimization Concierge.
- Solutions Eng Advisory (41-80): SE performs a deeper audit, runs representative workloads, suggests config bundles; target TTF contact <48h; owner: Solutions Eng.
- Runtime Engineering Escalation (81-120): Suspected runtime/kernel/KV changes required; create ENG ticket with reproducible perf repro and attach traces; owner: Serving Runtime team.
- Enterprise SLA Track (override if enterprise + SLA): Engage Customer Success + Solutions Eng + PM; propose committed timeline and optional Dedicated/Private route.

Automation approach:
Phase 1 (MVP rule-based): implement lookup + scoring inside Console intake endpoint. Expose a preview of recommended knobs and estimated cost delta using simple heuristics (batch size, seq len, quantization class).
Phase 2: train lightweight classifier using historical closed advisory tickets and outcomes; evaluate precision/recall; roll into auto-routing.

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form prototype available in Console staging with fields above.
- Rule-based scorer implemented and returns lane and score in API response.
- 3 internal pilot customers routed correctly (manual verification).
- Metrics dashboard created: auto-route rate, time-to-first-contact by lane, average score distribution, resolution time, estimated $ saved per closed ticket.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: deploy intake form to staging, internal pilot with 3 customer SRE/SE teams.
- Week 2: collect feedback, adjust thresholds and sample weights.
- Week 3: enable auto-routing for non-enterprise customers with manual reviewer notification.
- Week 4: enable Enterprise track auto-notify (manual SLA confirmation still required).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Overly aggressive cost-driven routing that suggests quantization causing quality regressions. Mitigation: require quality parity threshold and examples; Solutions Eng signoff for quantization >2-bit changes.
- Risk: Incomplete telemetry makes scores noisy. Mitigation: add required attachments for p95 and sample prompts; allow reviewer override and feedback loop to improve classifier.
